newsitem.title: GERMANY: Few worries for German monetary policy - wise men.
newsitem.headline: Few worries for German monetary policy - wise men.

text.p: German monetary policy is working well with inflation low this year at 1.5 percent, but the Bundesbank must work to keep price growth down next year, the five "wise men" panel of economic advisors said on Friday.
"With of stability so close, there is no urgent need to cut inflation further," the independent group of economists said in a report.
"But (the Bundesbank) must be on the alert to prevent an unexpectedly rapid growth in money supply from sowing the seed for problems late," it said.
Monetary growth will miss targets this year. The panel warned that with a monetary overhang, inflationary potential should not be underestimated.
The panel called for the Bundesbank to set an M3 growth target of 4.5 for 1997.
